commits.edited_message:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Merge segment reading.

Fixes #1470 by avoiding the second re-scanning.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Fix the segment merging.

The single bulk read also pulled the tag and size headers of the
following segments into the dictionary.  Read the payload of each
segment separately into the pre-sized block instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: Both commits rewrite the PFB branch of T1_Get_Private_Dict (src/type1/t1parse.c). The first commit ('Merge segment reading') introduces a sizing pass that totals the payload lengths of the 0x8002 binary segments, but its loop treats an empty binary segment as the end of the private dictionary (`tag != 0x8002U || !size`). In that commit this is harmless: the buffer allocation and the single bulk FT_STREAM_READ both use the same count, so reads never exceed the allocation (verified: tree with only this edit loads the probe input with a clean error, no ASan report). The second commit ('Fix the segment merging') replaces the bulk read with per-segment reads into the block pre-sized by the sizing pass. Its read loop has the plain, historically accurate shape (break only on a non-0x8002 tag); a zero-length segment is a natural no-op for it (FT_STREAM_READ of 0 bytes), so it silently skips past empty segments that stopped the sizing pass. On the real first commit (whose sizing pass has no early stop) the two passes always agree, so the second commit alone is also safe (verified: probe font loads and renders). Only in composition can the passes disagree: with a PFB whose eexec data places an empty 0x8002 segment between two non-empty ones, the block is sized for the segments before the empty one (64 bytes) while the read loop copies all of them (309 bytes), overflowing the heap buffer by 245 bytes in FT_STREAM_READ (ASan: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE at src/type1/t1parse.c:318, allocation at :305, reached via FT_New_Memory_Face -> T1_Open_Face -> T1_Get_Private_Dict). Fixing either single commit's diff removes the mismatch; neither diff is wrong on its own.
